understanding.purpose: Compare fiscal 2024 income-statement measures across four quarters and the full year, in USD millions.
understanding.reading: Readers scan each labeled row across to compare quarters and the annual total, and scan down a column to compare measures within a period. Row labels need enough space to remain recognizable as units.
groups: Q1–Q4 are parallel periods and should have equal widths to support comparison.
The full-year column summarizes the same measures across the four quarters and needs room for its longer heading.
The first column identifies each measure and needs more width for descriptive labels.
keep_intact: Quarterly and full-year numeric values, including decimal points.
Individual words in row labels where space permits.
may_wrap: Long row labels can wrap at word boundaries, especially the cost-of-revenue label.
The Full year heading can wrap between words.
The existing two-level header provides height for wrapped header text.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Try a middle ground between r1A and r1C. The label column should reduce the tallest row relative to r1C while bringing more of Q4 into view than r1A. Allow the full-year heading to wrap to save 13px.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Test an intermediate label width between r0A and r0C, seeking shorter label blocks without committing to r0C's full scrolling cost.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Use the minimum label width that accommodates the longest word, preserving whole words and numeric values while bringing more quarterly content into the initial viewport. Longer labels will require more lines.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Retain r1B's more readable labels and compact rows, while narrowing the annual column to reduce the total scroll distance. Its heading can wrap between words.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Reduce the label column from r2A to 145px to bring more of Q4 into the initial viewport while retaining enough width for individual words. Keep the quarter columns equal and numeric values intact.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give the label column the stated 115px minimum needed for its longest word. This tests whether almost all four quarters can appear initially without the visible word splits in r2C, accepting taller wrapped labels.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Use a label width between r2A and r2B and give Full year enough room on one line. This tests a more comfortable reading layout with greater horizontal scrolling.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: Fit the label column and all four quarters within 358px so the complete quarterly comparison appears initially. This deliberately accepts a split in the longest label word and taller rows; the annual total remains available by scrolling.
bad.why: The narrow row-header column splits words such as “depreciation” and “development” in the rendering. Its seven-line label also makes the row disproportionately tall.

rationale: r2A gives the long expense label enough room to remain readable while keeping the four quarter columns equal and their figures intact. Three quarters are visible initially, with part of Q4 indicating that more content lies to the right. The full-year heading wraps, but the narrower final column reduces the distance needed to reach it.

general: Give columns with the same comparison role consistent widths when their contents permit it.
Preserve whole words and numeric values, and judge wrapping by how well each row remains readable.
For a horizontally scrolling table, consider both the initial view and the distance to content outside it.
specific: The long expense label needs substantially more width than the quarterly figures.
Showing all four quarters initially requires a much narrower row-header column and produces a six-line expense label.
Wrapping the full-year heading saves horizontal space without breaking the heading's words.

tradeoffs: r3B shows all four quarterly figures at first sight and requires less scrolling, but its long row label takes six lines. r1B gives labels more space and keeps the full-year heading on one line, at the cost of substantially more scrolling.
uncertain: A designer prioritizing immediate comparison across all four quarters could reasonably prefer r3B. The ranges are approximate: nearby widths can change line breaks, so their visual equivalence should be checked in the renderer.

critique.good: The four equal quarterly columns keep values intact and establish a consistent comparison rhythm. The annual column has enough room for its heading and values. Row-label words remain intact.
critique.problems: The long cost-of-revenue label occupies four lines, making that row much taller than the others. Q4 is only partly visible at first sight, and the annual total requires horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 145px label column leaves 124px for text; the 62px quarterly columns and 82px annual column preserve their contents but bring the table to 476px.

critique.good: The entire table fits in the viewport, and the four quarters retain equal widths. The annual heading wraps naturally between words.
critique.problems: Numbers break across lines, making quarterly and annual values difficult to read and compare. Label words also split, and the resulting tall rows disrupt the relationship between labels and values.
critique.cause: Each 49px quarterly column leaves only 28px for text, and the 53px annual column leaves 32px. The 110px label column leaves 89px, less than the width of its longest word.

critique.good: Labels are easy to read, the cost-of-revenue label occupies only two lines, and all values and headings remain intact. The shorter, more even rows make comparisons comfortable once the relevant columns are in view.
critique.problems: The wide label column leaves only Q1 and part of Q2 visible initially. Readers must scroll substantially to compare the later quarters and annual total.
critique.cause: The 250px label column consumes most of the viewport, while the intact numeric columns extend the table to 581px.

critique.good: The labels remain intact, the quarterly columns have a consistent rhythm, and the annual heading fits on one line. Rows remain easy to follow across the table.
critique.problems: The cost-of-revenue label takes four lines, making that row noticeably tall. At first sight, the viewport shows only part of Q4, and the annual total requires scrolling.
critique.cause: The 175px label column leaves too little space for a more compact wrap of the long label. The four 62px quarter columns and 82px annual column bring the table to 506px.

critique.good: The wider label column reduces the cost-of-revenue label to three lines and gives the table a calmer vertical rhythm. Words and numbers remain intact, and the quarters are evenly sized.
critique.problems: The initial view reaches only partway through Q3, so comparing all four quarters requires a substantial horizontal scroll. The full-year column is farther away still.
critique.cause: The 200px label column improves wrapping but consumes more than half the viewport before the period columns begin. The 82px full-year column adds further width.

critique.good: All four quarters are nearly visible at first sight, and their equal widths make comparisons straightforward. Words and numeric values remain intact.
critique.problems: The long cost-of-revenue label breaks into six lines, while the other descriptive labels also become tall. The resulting row heights and narrow stack of words make the table harder to scan as a whole.
critique.cause: The 115px label column leaves only 94px for text, just enough for the longest individual word but too little for many words to share a line. The full-year column still requires scrolling.

critique.good: Equal quarter widths give the numeric columns a consistent rhythm. The row labels remain readable, and the full-year column has enough room for its values.
critique.problems: The cost-of-revenue row is tall, and the initial viewport shows only part of Q4; the full-year total requires horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 160px label column wraps the longest label over four lines, while the 478px total width exceeds the viewport by 118px.

critique.good: The wider label column gives the longest measure a more natural three-line wrap and produces the shortest, most compact table vertically. The quarter columns remain consistent.
critique.problems: The wide label column leaves only two quarters fully visible at first, with Q3 cut by the viewport and Q4 and the annual total farther offscreen.
critique.cause: The 200px label column consumes more than half the viewport and increases total overflow to 158px.

critique.good: All four quarter columns are visible at first, making quarter-to-quarter comparison easier. The total scroll distance is the smallest of the three.
critique.problems: The labels fragment severely: the render visibly splits “depreciation,” “amortization,” and “development” within words. The resulting tall rows make the table harder to scan, and the full-year column remains mostly offscreen.
critique.cause: At 110px, the label column has only 89px for text, less than the stated 94px longest unbreakable word. Its narrowness also forces many short lines.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r1C.why: The row labels wrap at word boundaries, and all four quarters are visible together. The full-year column requires horizontal scrolling.

ref_equal.why: Fitting all six columns into the viewport splits row labels and several numbers across lines, making comparisons difficult.

ref_auto.why: The labels remain readable and all four quarters fit in the initial view, though the full-year figures require scrolling.

r2C.why: The narrow label column splits words such as depreciation and development, interrupting the row labels. The full-year column still requires scrolling.

r1B.why: The wider label column gives the descriptions a comfortable rhythm, but only two quarters and part of a third appear initially, so comparing quarters requires more scrolling.

r2A.why: The labels wrap cleanly and three quarters are fully visible, though Q4 and the full-year figures require scrolling.

raw.unsure: A and C appear very similar at this scale; their full-year columns extend beyond the visible image, so their widths and any wrapping there cannot be assessed reliably.

r1B.why: Row labels wrap cleanly and remain easy to read, but only two complete quarter columns fit in the viewport; comparing the full year requires substantial horizontal scrolling.

r2A.why: Labels and values stay intact, and three complete quarters fit initially. The long cost label creates a tall row, and Q4 and the full-year total require scrolling.

ref_equal.why: The whole table fits, but row labels and several numbers split across lines, making both identification and numerical comparison difficult.

ref_auto.why: All four quarters fit initially, with intact numbers and readable labels. The full-year column lies mostly beyond the viewport, and the long cost label makes its row tall.

r2C.why: All four quarters fit, but words such as depreciation, amortization and development break within the row labels. The full-year column still requires scrolling.

r1C.why: All four quarters fit with intact numbers and readable row labels. The full-year column requires horizontal scrolling, and the long cost label makes its row tall.

raw.unsure: D and F look very similar at this scale; their full-year columns are largely outside the viewport, so small differences in their widths and off-screen wrapping are difficult to judge.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
